_README: Female-plumage manifest for the illustration pipeline's --sex female mode (pregen.py). Keys are scientific names; values are 1-2 sentence adult-FEMALE plumage notes injected into the prompt when rendering that species' female variant (<slug>-f.png / <slug>-f-2.png). Species absent from this file are treated as MONOMORPHIC: no female render is generated and the frontend shows only the male art. Only strongly dimorphic species belong here. Loaders skip keys starting with '_' (same convention as species-notes.json).
_built_during: 2026-07-27 illustration-sex-variants plan (todo 1); 41 species = 19 dimorphic birds heard on the live Pi + 22 curated dimorphic Ontario species
Cardinalis cardinalis: Adult FEMALE: warm buff-brown overall with reddish tinges on crest, wings, and tail; face mask subdued dark gray, not bold black; coral-red bill.
Haemorhous mexicanus: Adult FEMALE: streaky brown-gray overall with heavily streaked underparts and a blurred pale eyebrow; NO red anywhere.
Spinus tristis: Adult FEMALE: breeding female: olive-yellow above, dull yellow below, blackish wings with two buffy wing bars; NO black cap.
Passer domesticus: Adult FEMALE: a small plump plainly-colored bird: uniform warm buff-brown above, entirely plain sandy-buff head and underparts with one broad cream eyebrow stripe, small conical bill, streaked brown back and wings. Render the head and underparts as ONE flat sandy-buff color zone with no internal markings at all - the only dark ink lines on the head are the eye, the eyebrow stripe, and the bill outline. Head pattern CRITICAL: plain buff-brown crown, NO chestnut/rufous crown, NO black cheek spot, NO black bib - Eurasian Tree Sparrow head markings are WRONG. The sparrow shown in the IMAGE 1 photo is the correct species and sex: copy its plain buff head exactly. The classic kachō-e woodblock sparrow is the Eurasian Tree Sparrow (Passer montanus), a DIFFERENT species with a rufous crown, white cheeks, black cheek spot, and black bib - do NOT paint that species' head pattern here. The sparrows in any style print are also that different species - borrow only their painting technique, NEVER their facial markings.
Sialia sialis: Adult FEMALE: grayish-blue above (much duller than male), gray head, pale rusty wash across breast, pale belly. TONAL REQUIREMENT (critical): every pale area - throat edges, lower breast, belly, vent, undertail coverts - must be painted in a CLEARLY VISIBLE warm grey-buff wash at least two tonal steps darker than the cream ground, about the depth of weak tea or light oatmeal; NEVER pure white, NEVER near-white, NEVER the same value as the background. The entire belly and vent must read as one solid opaque painted shape fully enclosed by the bird's continuous dark ink outline, with a visible tonal boundary against the ground everywhere. Absolutely no twig, branch, or perch - feet free.
Turdus migratorius: Adult FEMALE: paler gray-brown head (not blackish), duller orange breast, faint dark streaking on the white throat.
Quiscalus quiscula: Adult FEMALE: smaller than male, dull brown overall with only faint iridescence; pale yellow eye.
Sitta carolinensis: Adult FEMALE: like the male but the cap is dull gray-black (not glossy jet black) and the rusty underparts are paler.
Sitta canadensis: Adult FEMALE: duller than male: gray-brown (not jet-black) cap and eye-line, paler cinnamon underparts.
Chordeiles minor: Adult FEMALE: buffy (not white) throat patch, NO white tail band, narrower buffy wing bar. Nightjar anatomy CRITICAL: tiny bill, very long pointed wings, long tail, cryptic buff-barred plumage, buffy throat patch, NO cuckoo features (no long decurved bill, no cuckoo proportions). Head CRITICAL: a large flat head with huge dark eyes and a MINUSCULE flat bill sitting on an enormous gape, the mouth line running back under the eye - NOT a conical seed-eater bill. Face plain and cryptic - NO bold pale supercilium, NO dark eye-stripe, NO dark malar stripe, NO passerine face mask. Not a bunting.
Melanerpes carolinus: Adult FEMALE: red ONLY on the nape; the crown is gray (the male's red extends from nape to bill).
Dryobates pubescens: Adult FEMALE: the head is strictly black-and-white with NO red, orange, or rufous anywhere on the head (no nape patch, no lore patch); otherwise the same black-and-white pattern as the male.
Dryobates villosus: Adult FEMALE: NO red patch on the back of the head; otherwise the same black-and-white pattern.
Dryocopus pileatus: Adult FEMALE: red crest only, with a BLACK-brown forehead (not red) and a BLACK (not red) moustache stripe. Female head CRITICAL: red crest ONLY; forehead BLACK-brown, moustache stripe BLACK - no red on forehead or malar. Body sooty black-brown (not blue-grey); woodpecker zygodactyl foot, two toes forward.
Aix sponsa: Adult FEMALE: gray-brown overall, bold white teardrop eye patch, dark crested head with white throat, flanks finely streaked; NO bold male pattern.
Anas platyrhynchos: Adult FEMALE: mottled buff-brown overall, orange saddle on a dark bill, blue speculum edged in white, orange legs.
Meleagris gallopavo: Adult FEMALE: a slim small-headed turkey in a relaxed horizontal feeding posture with the head held low and forward: smooth brown-gray barred plumage over the entire body, small sparsely-feathered blue-gray head and neck, muted faint iridescence. The chest and breast form one smooth unbroken rounded outline from chin to belly.
Geothlypis trichas: Adult FEMALE: olive-brown above, bright yellow throat and undertail coverts, NO black mask, pale broken eye-ring.
Pandion haliaetus: Adult FEMALE: heavier dark streaking across the upper breast forming a distinct necklace bib; otherwise like the male.
Agelaius phoeniceus: Adult FEMALE: dark brown overall, heavily streaked below, bold pale eyebrow, rusty-buff wash on face and throat; NO red epaulets, NO glossy black.
Molothrus ater: Adult FEMALE: plain gray-brown overall, paler below with faint streaking, dark eye, pointed conical bill.
Icterus galbula: Adult FEMALE: olive-yellow above, dull orange-yellow below, grayish wings with two white wing bars; NO black head.
Icterus spurius: Adult FEMALE: olive-green above, yellow below, two whitish wing bars; NO black hood, NO chestnut.
Passerina cyanea: Adult FEMALE: warm cinnamon-brown overall with a faint blue tinge in wings and tail and two buffy wing bars; NO all-blue plumage.
Pheucticus ludovicianus: Adult FEMALE: brown above with bold buffy eyebrow and crown stripes, heavily streaked underparts and back, pinkish bill; NO rose breast.
Piranga olivacea: Adult FEMALE: olive-yellow overall, yellowish below, wings dull olive (not black), stout pale bill; NO scarlet.
Archilochus colubris: Adult FEMALE: green above, clean white below, NO ruby gorget; white-tipped outer tail feathers.
Sphyrapicus varius: Adult FEMALE: white (not red) throat; red crown; otherwise the same black-and-white barred pattern.
Setophaga petechia: Adult FEMALE: plain bright yellow overall with NO chestnut breast streaks; yellow wing bars, dark eye.
Setophaga ruticilla: Adult FEMALE: gray-olive above, whitish below, with yellow (not orange-red) patches on the sides, wings, and tail base.
Setophaga magnolia: Adult FEMALE: duller gray-olive above, yellow rump, faint gray necklace streaks, white wing patches, white undertail with a dark band.
Setophaga caerulescens: Adult FEMALE: olive-green above, buffy-white below, small white wing patch, thin white eye-arc; NO blue upperparts, NO black throat.
Setophaga castanea: Adult FEMALE: olive-gray above, pale yellow wash below with faint streaking, two wing bars, pale eye-ring; NO bay breast, NO black mask. Field marks CRITICAL: TWO BOLD pale wing bars on EACH wing (essential - do not omit) - on the spread wing they are two pale bars across the dark flight feathers, formed by the pale tips of the greater and median wing coverts, one bar above the other, clearly visible on each wing in flight; the wings are NEVER plain unmarked dark gray. Head plain olive-gray, concolorous with the back - NO slate-gray hood, NO gray cheeks; eye-ring thin and inconspicuous, NOT a bold complete white ring; breast and flanks with FAINT dark streaking; throat the same pale yellow wash as the breast - NO peach, salmon, or buff color block on the throat. Do NOT paint a Nashville Warbler: no plain slate-gray hood, no bold complete white eye-ring, no unstreaked yellow underparts - wing bars are REQUIRED.
Setophaga coronata: Adult FEMALE: browner than the male with a streaked breast; keeps the yellow rump and yellow side patches; NO crisp black face and bib.
Loxia leucoptera: Adult FEMALE: yellow-olive and heavily streaked (not pink-red), two bold white wing bars, crossed mandibles.
Mergus serrator: Adult FEMALE: gray body, shaggy reddish-brown head with a clean white chin patch, slender red bill. Underparts: a clean pale grey-buff breast and belly, at least two tonal steps darker than the cream ground (depth of weak tea), never white. TONAL REQUIREMENT (critical): every pale area - chin, throat, breast, belly, vent, flanks, and the pale wing patch - must be painted in a CLEARLY VISIBLE pale grey-buff wash at least two tonal steps darker than the cream ground; never pure white, never near-white, never the same value as the background. The whole pale underbody must read as one solid opaque painted shape fully enclosed by the bird's continuous dark ink outline, with a visible tonal edge separating the belly from the ground everywhere.
Clangula hyemalis: Adult FEMALE: winter plumage: brown body and short tail (NO long central streamers); the head is mostly WHITE - white face and cheeks with a dark brown crown and a single dark cheek smudge - do NOT render a dark hood or dark face.
Aythya marila: Adult FEMALE: brown body, bold white face patch at the base of the bill, gray back, yellow eye, blue-gray bill with black tip.
Dolichonyx oryzivorus: Adult FEMALE: buffy overall with a heavily streaked back and breast and bold head stripes; NO black-and-white male pattern.
Haemorhous purpureus: Adult FEMALE: brown and heavily streaked overall with a bold whitish eyebrow and dark cheek patch; NO raspberry red anywhere.
Falco sparverius: Adult FEMALE: rufous back AND wings with black barring (the male's wings are slate-blue), streaked buff breast; same bold face stripes.
